title: Missale Chaldaicum (Rome Propaganda, 1767) — Anaphora of Addai and Mari Core — independent pixel-collation review
scope: Bounded constituent of the eight core prayers of the Anaphora of Addai and Mari (Opening Dialogue, Preface Gehanta 1, Sanctus, Post-Sanctus Gehanta 2, Intercession Gehanta 3, Anamnesis/Oblation, Epiclesis, and Fraction-placed Institution Narrative) in Classical Syriac (syr), excluding private Kushapa prayers, rubrics, and intervening fraction prayers.
method: Independent pixel-level visual inspection of all rendered facsimile pages by independent-collator-v2-syriac (distinct from drafter lane-t2-syriac) on 2026-11-25. Applied 6 pixel-verified correction(s) relative to initial draft; verified every unit boundary, page account (1..634), and SHA-256 hash.
normalization_limit: Pure consonantal Classical Syriac Unicode (U+0710..U+072C, UTF-8 NFC) with single ASCII spaces between words and single LF (\n) line endings, one canonical liturgical unit per line.; All East Syriac and West Syriac vowel points, seyame (U+0308), qushshaya/rukkakha, linea occultans/marhetana, punctuation dots, liturgical crosses, quotation marks, kashidas, catchwords, running heads, signature marks, and page numbers are omitted for scan-safe cross-edition diffing.; Rubrics (red or black stage directions), section headers (e.g. Qanona, Gehanta), speaker labels (priest/deacon/people), abbreviated posture cues (e.g. gehanta bow marker), intervening private Kushapa prayers, diaconal calls outside the main dialogue, and parallel Garshuni/Arabic columns are excluded.; Printed historical orthography, abbreviations (such as abbreviated Sanctus incipits), omissions, and additions are preserved verbatim without harmonizing or supplying words from memory.
review_limit: Complete declared constituent only, not whole-book transcription or diplomatic typography.
